title: Grade 3 Science — Fri, Jun 13
description: Plant Kingdom — Day 5 of 5: Mixed review — plants we eat, medicinal plants, trees/shrubs/herbs
subject: science

questions.question: A tall plant with a hard, thick trunk and branches is called a:
questions.explanation: Trees are tall plants with one thick, hard woody trunk. Examples: mango, banyan, neem, and peepal.

questions.question: A plant that is small and has many thin woody branches from the base is called a:
questions.explanation: Shrubs have multiple thin woody stems from the base and are shorter than trees. Examples: rose, hibiscus, cotton.

questions.question: A small, soft-stemmed plant used in cooking (like mint, coriander, or tulsi) is called a:
questions.explanation: Herbs are small plants with soft, non-woody stems. Many herbs like mint, basil, and coriander are used in Indian cooking.

questions.question: Tulsi (Holy Basil) is a medicinal plant. It is used to:
questions.explanation: Tulsi is sacred in Hindu homes and is also a powerful medicinal herb used to treat colds, coughs, and fever.

questions.question: Neem is called the 'village pharmacy' because:
options: Its leaves, bark, and seeds are used to treat many diseases
It produces fruit that pharmacists eat
questions.explanation: Neem has powerful anti-bacterial and anti-fungal properties. Its twigs, leaves, and oil are used for dental care, skin problems, and more.

questions.question: Which of these do we eat the leaf of?
questions.explanation: Spinach (palak) is a leafy vegetable — we eat its leaves. Potato is a stem, radish is a root, groundnut is a seed.

questions.question: We eat the fruit of which of these plants?
questions.explanation: We eat the fruit of the mango tree. Carrot is a root, ginger is a stem, and spinach is a leaf.

questions.question: We eat the seeds of:
questions.explanation: Wheat and rice grains are seeds. Seeds are rich in nutrients and are a primary food source for humans.

questions.question: Aloe vera is a plant known for:
options: Its gel that soothes skin burns and is used in medicines
questions.explanation: Aloe vera gel from its thick leaves soothes sunburns and skin irritation. It is widely used in cosmetics and Ayurvedic medicine.

questions.question: Which of these is a climbing plant?
questions.explanation: Pumpkin vines are climbers — they use their tendrils to climb over fences and walls. Cucumber and beans are also climbers.

questions.question: Which type of plant is the smallest — tree, shrub, or herb?
questions.explanation: Herbs are the smallest. They have soft stems and are short-lived. Shrubs are medium-sized. Trees are the tallest.

questions.question: The banyan tree has branches that grow down to the ground as additional roots. This makes it:
options: Very wide — the widest tree on Earth in some cases
questions.explanation: The Great Banyan Tree in Kolkata's botanical garden is considered the widest living tree in the world, covering several acres.

questions.question: Which plants can survive in deserts with very little water?
questions.explanation: Cacti and succulents store water in their thick stems or leaves. Their leaves are modified as spines to reduce water loss.

questions.question: Ginger, turmeric, and garlic are all examples of:
options: Medicinal plants also used as spices in Indian cooking
questions.explanation: Ginger, turmeric, and garlic are medicinal plants used as spices and home remedies in India for centuries.

questions.question: Which part of a plant does NOT contain chlorophyll and so is usually white or brown?
questions.explanation: Roots are underground and have no sunlight, so they do not make chlorophyll. They are typically white or light-coloured.
